# Simulate one generation

There was an error because some values were negative. That's why we put the max() at some places.

```{r}
# Simulate WT-Population without any mutations and stochasticity
simulate_one_gen <- function(N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu){
  N_a0 <- max(N_a0, 0) #we use max to avoid negative 
  New_jtM <- max(rpois(1, N_a0 * mu * R_a), 0) #New Juvenile mutants
  N_jt <- max(rpois(1, R_a * N_a0) - New_jtM, 0) #calculating number of WT juvenile individual
  
  N_at <- max(rpois(1, S_j * N_j0 + S_a * N_a0), 0) #calculating number of adult individuals
  
  
  N_jtM <- max(rpois(1, N_a0M * R_aM) + New_jtM, 0) # calculating number of Mutant juveniles
  N_atM <- max (rpois(1, N_j0M * S_jM + S_aM * N_a0M), 0) # calculating number of Mutant adults
  
  return(c(N_jt, N_at, N_jtM, N_atM))
}

```

## Simulate a population trajectory

```{r}
simulate_pop <- function(N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu, t_max) {
   # Create the vector in which to save the results
  pop_vector <- c(N_j0, N_a0, N_j0M, N_a0M) 
  # initiate the variables
  pop_new <- c(N_j0, N_a0, N_j0M, N_a0M)
  
  # run the simulation until generation t_max
  for (i in 1:t_max+1) {
    # redefine the current population one generation later
    pop_new <- simulate_one_gen(pop_new[1],pop_new[2],pop_new[3],pop_new[4], R_a,R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu)
    
    # add the new population sizes to the output vector
    pop_vector <- rbind(pop_vector,pop_new)
    # condition to stop the simulation before t_max: either the population exceeds 10 times the original population size, or it goes extinct
    if ( (pop_new[1]+pop_new[2]+ pop_new[3]+pop_new[4] >=10*(N_j0+ N_a0 + N_j0M+ N_a0M)) | (pop_new[1]+pop_new[2]+ pop_new[3]+pop_new[4]==0)) break }
  
  # add row and column names
  colnames(pop_vector) <- c("AC1", "AC2", "AC1M", "AC2M")
  rownames(pop_vector) <- (0:t_max)[1:length(pop_vector[,1])]
  
  return(pop_vector)
}


```

## Compare juvenile- vs. adult survival rate increase in mutants

We have to figure out which ranges of survival rates make sense. So the growth rate of the wildtypes should be below 1 and for the mutants it should be more than 1 probably.

```{r}
# set some parameters to fixed values

N_j0 <-50
N_a0 <- 50
N_j0M <- 0
N_a0M <- 0
R_a <- 2
R_aM <- 2
S_j <- 0.2
S_a <- 0.5
mu <- 0.01
t_max <- 1000



# determine how often to run the simulation for each set of parameters
no_replicates <- 1000

# initialize data table - where to collect the results
data_table_survcompare <- c()

# Doing a parameter sweep
for (selection_on_jM in c(TRUE,FALSE)){
  for (s_coeff in seq(1, 2, 0.05)){
    S_j <- 0.2
    S_jM <- S_j * ifelse(selection_on_jM, s_coeff, 1)
    S_a <- 0.5
    S_aM <- S_a * ifelse(selection_on_jM, 1, s_coeff)
  
   
    i<-1
    repeat {
      # increase counter by one
      i<-i+1
      # run the simulation once
      one_run <- simulate_pop(N_j0, N_a0,N_j0M, N_a0M, R_a, R_aM, S_j, S_jM, S_a, S_aM, mu, t_max)
      # determine total population sizes
      total_size <- one_run[,1]+one_run[,2] +one_run[,3]+one_run[,4]
      # determine minimum population size
      min_size <- min(total_size)
      # determine (first) generation at which this population size occurred
      min_gen <- as.numeric(which(total_size==min_size)[1])
      #adding absollute survival
      S_abs <- ifelse(selection_on_jM, S_jM, S_aM)
      # enter the data into the table
      data_table_survcompare <- rbind(data_table_survcompare,c(s_coeff,S_abs,ifelse(selection_on_jM, "on_juveniles", "on_adults"),min_gen,min_size)) # note that we add the varying parameters (decay rate and selection coefficient) to the table too
      # stop the repeated computation after no_replicates times
      if(i>no_replicates) break
    }
  }  
}
 
# define column names of data table
colnames(data_table_survcompare) <- c("S_coeff","S_absolute","ac_s","min_gen","no_min")
# show the first lines of the output


#making the matrix a table and making some values numeric to be able to calculate with them
df <- as.data.frame(data_table_survcompare)
df$S_abs <- as.numeric(df$S_abs)
df$min_gen <- as.numeric(df$min_gen)
df$no_min <- as.numeric(df$no_min)

df$rescued <- df$no_min != 0

#try if the basic principle of getting the rescue-probability works
df_filter <- df[df$s_coeff == 1 & df$ac_s == "on_juveniles",]

#creating a empty table to put the stuff to plot in
plot_table <- c()
for(x in unique(df$ac_s)){
 for(s in unique(df$S_abs)){
  df_filter <- df[df$S_abs == s & df$ac_s == x,]
  plot_table <- rbind(plot_table, c(mean(df_filter$rescued), x, s))
 } 
}

colnames(plot_table) <- c("rescue prob.","ac_s","S_absolute")



```

## comparing mutated reproduction rate vs mutated survival rate, combination of reproduction rates and survivability rates.

```{r}

# --- 1. BASE PARAMETERS ---
N_j0 <-50
N_a0 <- 50
N_j0M <- 0
N_a0M <- 0
R_a <- 2
S_j <- 0.2
S_a <- 0.5
mu <- 0.01
t_max <- 1000



# Simulation repetitions
no_replicates <- 100

#data table initializing
data_table <- c()

# loop over reproduction selection
for (repro_val in seq(1,1.5,0.05)) {
  
  # loop over survival selection
  for (surv_val in seq(1, 1.2, 0.02)) {
    
    # Calculate modified rates based on current loop values 
    current_R_aM <- R_a * repro_val
    current_S_aM <- S_a * surv_val
    current_S_jM <- S_j * surv_val
    
    # reset counter for replicates
    i <- 1
    
    repeat {
      # run the simulation once with the modified parameters
      one_run <- simulate_pop(N_j0, N_a0, N_j0M, N_a0M, 
                              R_a, current_R_aM, 
                              S_j, current_S_jM, 
                              S_a, current_S_aM, 
                              mu, t_max)
      
      # determine total population sizes
      total_size <- one_run[,1] + one_run[,2] + one_run[,3] + one_run[,4]
      
      # determine minimum population size
      min_size <- min(total_size)
      
  
      # determine (first) generation at which this population size occurred
      min_gen <- as.numeric(which(total_size == min_size)[1])
      
      
      
      # enter the data into the table
      data_table <- rbind(data_table, c(repro_val, surv_val, min_gen, min_size, current_R_aM,current_S_aM))
      
      # stop the repeated computation after no_replicates times
      if (i >= no_replicates) break
      
      # increase counter by one
      i <- i + 1
    }
  }
}

# define column names of data table
colnames(data_table) <- c("repro_multiplier", "surv_multiplier", "min_gen", "min_size", "Current_R", "Current_S_Juveniles")

# Convert to data frame
data_table_RvsS <- as.data.frame(data_table)
# Add "rescued" column
data_table_RvsS$rescued <- data_table_RvsS$min_size != 0



summary_table <- c()
for(x in unique(data_table_RvsS$Current_R)){
  for(s in unique(data_table_RvsS$Current_S)){
    data_table_filter <- data_table_RvsS[data_table_RvsS$Current_R == x & data_table_RvsS$Current_S == s,]
    summary_table <- rbind(summary_table, c(mean(data_table_filter$rescued), x, s))
  } 
}

colnames(summary_table) <- c("rescue probability","Reproduction rate", "Current_S")



```

## matrix thing to keep the lambda constant

```{r}
# 1. Define resident matrix
# define WT leslie matrix and get growth rate
  l_matrix_WT <- matrix(c(
    0, R_a,
    S_j, S_a
  ), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  
  all_eigen <- eigen(l_matrix_WT)
  growth_rate_WT <- max(Re(all_eigen$values))
  l_matrix_WT
  growth_rate_WT

# define Mut leslie matrix and getting growth rate
  R_aM <- 1.5 * R_a
  S_jM <- 1.2 * S_j
  S_aM <- 1.2 * S_a
  l_matrix_Mut <- matrix(c(
    0, R_aM,
    S_jM, S_aM
  ), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  
  all_eigen <- eigen(l_matrix_Mut)
  growth_rate_Mut <- max(Re(all_eigen$values))
  l_matrix_Mut
  growth_rate_Mut

# 2. Function to compute required reproduction multiplier (reproduction_advantage) for a given survival multiplier (survival_advantage)
  find_repro_multiplier <- function(survival_advantage, matrix, target_lambda) {
    F1 <- matrix[1, 1]
    F2 <- matrix[1, 2]
    P1 <- matrix[2, 1]
    P2 <- matrix[2, 2]
    
    num <- target_lambda^2 - survival_advantage * P2 * target_lambda
    den <- F1 * target_lambda - survival_advantage * (F1 * P2 - F2 * P1)
    
    return(num / den)
  }
```

## Testing the equation for the probability of evolutionary rescue through a new mutation

The Equation: $P_{new} = 1 - e^{-\frac{2N_0 u (s - r)}{r}}$

The parameters

- $P_{new}$ : Probability of Evolutionary Rescue

- $N_0$: Initial population size

- $u$: mutation rate

- $s$: selection coefficient (advantage of mutant relative to WT)

- $r$: decay rate (1-initial growth rate)

### How the parameters translate to our model

- Selection coefficient ($s$): This would be the lambda of the Mutant Leslie Matrix minus the lambda of the WT-Leslie Matrix.

- decay rate ($r$): 1 - The lambda of the WT-Leslie Matrix

- The other parameters are unchanged in our model and we keep them as they are.

### How to test the equation

The same lambda can be achieved with different matrices. So in our case with different values for the Reproduction- and Survival rates. To really know if the rescue probability of the population in our model can be explained only by the lambda + the other parameters on the right side of the equation we would need to test for different combinations of Reproduction- / Survival-rates. For that we could use the code used above to quantify the importance of a higher reproduction in the mutants vs. a higher survival.

### Actual coding

#### Creating "summary_table"

The initial code gives a table called "summary_table", which contains:

- **Rescue Probability**

- **repro_multiplie**r: A number higher than 1 with which the reproduction rate of the WT-Adults is multiplied to get the reproduction rate of the Mutant-Adults. The initial reproduction rate was 2.

- **surv_multiplier**: A number higher than 1 with which the survival rates of the WT-Adults and Juveniles is multiplied to get the survival rates of the Mutant-Adults and Juveniles. The initial survival rates were 0.2 for the juveniles and 0.5 for the adults.

#### Getting the corresponding selection coefficient + initial growth rate

For the equation i need to calculate the selection coefficient + the initial growth rate of the population. These can be derived from the parameters "$R_a$", "$S_j$",, "$S_a$", "repro_val" and "surv_val".

#### Calculating the "$P_{new}$" with the equation: $P_{new} = 1 - e^{-\frac{2N_0 u (s - r)}{r}}$ for each row in summary_table

#### Deleting all rows where s is not \> than r

```{r}

# --- 1. BASE PARAMETERS ---
N_j0 <-50
N_a0 <- 50
N_j0M <- 0
N_a0M <- 0
R_a <- 2
S_j <- 0.17
S_a <- 0.3
mu <- 0.01
t_max <- 1000



# Simulation repetitions
no_replicates <- 100

#data table initializing
data_table <- c()

# loop over reproduction selection
for (repro_val in seq(1,1.5,0.05)) {
  
  # loop over survival selection
  for (surv_val in seq(1, 2, 0.1)) {
    
    # Calculate modified rates based on current loop values
    current_R_aM <- R_a * repro_val
    current_S_aM <- S_j * surv_val
    current_S_jM <- S_a * surv_val
    
    # reset counter for replicates
    i <- 1
    
    repeat {
      # run the simulation once with the modified parameters
      one_run <- simulate_pop(N_j0, N_a0, N_j0M, N_a0M, 
                              R_a, current_R_aM, 
                              S_j, current_S_jM, 
                              S_a, current_S_aM, 
                              mu, t_max)
      
      # determine total population sizes
      total_size <- one_run[,1] + one_run[,2] + one_run[,3] + one_run[,4]
      
      # determine minimum population size
      min_size <- min(total_size)
      
      # determine (first) generation at which this population size occurred
      min_gen <- as.numeric(which(total_size == min_size)[1])
      
      # enter the data into the table
      data_table <- rbind(data_table, c(repro_val, surv_val, min_gen, min_size))
      
      # stop the repeated computation after no_replicates times
      if (i >= no_replicates) break
      
      # increase counter by one
      i <- i + 1
    }
  }
}

# define column names of data table
colnames(data_table) <- c("repro_multiplier", "surv_multiplier", "min_gen", "min_size")

# Convert to data frame
data_table_analysis <- as.data.frame(data_table)
# Add "rescued" column
data_table_analysis$rescued <- data_table_analysis$min_size != 0



summary_table <- c()
for(x in unique(data_table_analysis$repro_multiplier)){
  for(s in unique(data_table_analysis$surv_multiplier)){
    data_table_filter <- data_table_analysis[data_table_analysis$repro_multiplier == x & data_table_analysis$surv_multiplier == s,]
    summary_table <- rbind(summary_table, c(mean(data_table_filter$rescued), x, s))
  } 
}

colnames(summary_table) <- c("resque probability", "repro_multiplier", "surv_multiplier")
summary_table <- as.data.frame(summary_table)
# the initial r-value is the same for all
  # define WT leslie matrix, get growth rate and define "r"
  l_matrix_WT <- matrix(c(
    0, R_a,
    S_j, S_a
  ), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
  
  all_eigen <- eigen(l_matrix_WT)
  growth_rate_WT <- max(Re(all_eigen$values))
  l_matrix_WT
  r <-  1 - growth_rate_WT
  r

# here i want to add the corresponding s-values to the summary_table
  # Calculate difference in days, then convert to approximate years
  # make function to generally get the selection_coefficient
    # first create a new column for the summary_table
    summary_table$selection_coefficient <- 0
    
    get_s <- function(R_a, S_j, S_a, summary_table, r, growth_rate_WT){
      selection_coefficients <- c()
      for (i in 1:nrow(summary_table)) {
        #make the current matrix and calculate the current_mut_r
        R_aM <- R_a * summary_table[i, "repro_multiplier"]
        S_jM <- S_j * summary_table[i, "surv_multiplier"]
        S_aM <- S_a * summary_table[i, "surv_multiplier"]
        current_l_matrix_Mut <- matrix(c(
          0, R_aM,
          S_jM, S_aM
        ), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
        
        all_eigen <- eigen(current_l_matrix_Mut)
        current_mut_r <- max(Re(all_eigen$values))
        
        current_selection_coefficient <- current_mut_r - growth_rate_WT
        
        summary_table[i, "selection_coefficient"] <- current_selection_coefficient
        print(current_selection_coefficient)
        
      }
      return(summary_table)
    }
    
    summary_table <- get_s(R_a, S_j, S_a, summary_table, r, growth_rate_WT)
    
# now i wan't to calculate the P_new and add it to the summary_table
    summary_table$rescue_probability_equation <- 0
    N_0 <- N_a0 + N_a0M + N_j0 + N_j0M
    add_p_new <- function(N_0, mu, r, summary_table){
      for (i in 1:nrow(summary_table)){
        s <- summary_table[i, "selection_coefficient"]
        P_new <- 1 - exp(-(2*N_0*mu*(s-r))/(r))
        summary_table[i, "rescue_probability_equation"] <- P_new
      }
     return(summary_table)
    }
    
  summary_table <- add_p_new(N_0, mu, r, summary_table)
  
  # 1. Calculate mutant lambda (growth_rate_WT + s)
  summary_table$lambda_mutant <- growth_rate_WT + summary_table$selection_coefficient
  
  # 2. Filter out negative estimated rescue probabilities and reshape for plotting
  plot_data <- summary_table %>%
    filter(rescue_probability_equation >= 0) %>%
    rename(Simulated = `resque probability`, Formula = rescue_probability_equation) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(Simulated, Formula),
      names_to = "Source",
      values_to = "Rescue_Probability"
    )
  
  # 3. Create the plot
  ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = lambda_mutant, y = Rescue_Probability, color = Source)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
    geom_smooth(se = FALSE, method = "loess", span = 0.8) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(
      title = "Evolutionary Rescue Probability vs. Mutant Growth Rate",
      x = expression(paste("Mutant Growth Rate (", lambda[mut], ")")),
      y = "Rescue Probability",
      color = "Type"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("Simulated" = "steelblue", "Formula" = "darkorange")) +
    ylim(0, 1)
```
